1. Query the atlas

Source: vignettes/query_the_atlas.Rmd
query_the_atlas.Rmd

This page is the script for the first block. Run the code in your R session, in order.

This practice takes Human Cell Atlas data from CELLxGENE. Each study is a table of measurements at single cell level (one row per cell). cellNexus makes that query reusable and fast at the sample level. It also adds three cell-type labels with SingleR, using the Blueprint, Monaco, and Azimuth references. A harmonisation step then combines those three labels into one unified cell-type label for every cell. The diagram below shows the preprocessing steps, starting from the original CELLxGENE data.

Setup 

library(cellNexus)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(cellNexusWorkshop)

get_metadata() returns a lazy DuckDB table. Filters stay in the query until something collects the rows, which is what makes an atlas of this size practical to subset.

metadata <- get_metadata() |>
  keep_quality_cells()

keep_quality_cells() applies one gate and filters out bad quality cells from every sample.

  • An empty droplet is liquid captured with almost no cell in it. It still produces a few gene measurements, mostly background. Counting it as a cell inflates the number of cells and adds noise.
  • A dead cell is detected by a high mitochondrial percentage.
  • A doublet is two cells captured together. Their measurements are mixed, so the row can look like a cell type that does not exist.

The same checks are computed for each sample. Detailed information on the procedure is the cellNexus quality-control steps.

Choose cells by cell type

cell_type_unified_ensemble is the harmonised label (multi-reference consensus annotation). age_days and imputed_ethnicity are sample-level fields.

Exploring the harmonised cell types in the atlas.

metadata |>
  dplyr::distinct(cell_type_unified_ensemble) |>
  dplyr::arrange(cell_type_unified_ensemble)

  dplyr::count(imputed_ethnicity, sort = TRUE)

Exercise 1. Count cells per cell_type_unified_ensemble for donors older than 50 years (age_days > 50 * 365). Which labels are rare enough that a proportion estimated from 50 cells would be mostly sampling noise?

Solution 
library(cellNexus)
library(dplyr)

get_metadata() |>
  keep_quality_cells() |>
  dplyr::filter(age_days > 50 * 365) |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, sort = TRUE)

A label with a few dozen cells across the whole atlas will have a very wide composition interval. Drop it from the cell-type list, or accept that its estimate is descriptive.

This case study uses nine respiratory reference studies in particular. join_census_tissue() appends CELLxGENE Census demographic annotations such as tissue, disease, sex, age_days, etc to the metadata.

Build the respiratory ageing cohort

Immune and epithelial cell types are queried. Age is restricted to donors from 1 year up to 80 years, which drops perinatal samples and donors who would fall outside the age bins.

cell_types_query <- c(immune_cell_types(), epithelial_cell_types())

obs_lung <- get_metadata() |>
  keep_quality_cells() |>
  dplyr::filter(
    dataset_id %in% dataset_ids,
    cell_type_unified_ensemble %in% cell_types_query,
    age_days >= 365,
    age_days < 80 * 365
  ) |>
  join_census_tissue() |>
  annotate_cell_nexus(min_cells_per_sample = 50)

obs_lung |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, name = "n_cells") |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(n_cells))
## # A tibble: 29 × 2
##    cell_type_unified_ensemble n_cells
##    <chr>                        <int>
##  1 macrophage                  196975
##  2 epithelial                  183063
##  3 pneumocyte                  156299
##  4 cd14 mono                    45990
##  5 secretory                    39620
##  6 nk                           37230
##  7 cd8 tem                      34201
##  8 plasma                       23810
##  9 cdc                          13773
## 10 mast                         13578
## # ℹ 19 more rows

join_census_tissue() attaches Census tissue. annotate_cell_nexus() keeps the respiratory labels, collects the query, derives the age variables, drops samples with fewer than 50 cells, and de-duplicates on observation_joinid. Every cell of every retained sample is kept. sccomp conditions on each sample’s total, and the expression model carries library size as a covariate, so equal-size subsampling would throw away precision.

age_binary is TRUE for donors older than 50 years. age_bin is the same split, labelled for plots. One encoding means the composition model and the expression model contrast the same donors. The boundary is a modelling choice: report it, and check that both sides are populated.

Inspect the cohort before modelling

Look at the age histogram and the cell-type bar chart before fitting a model. Both age classes should contain donors. Ages clumped into two distant groups will make a continuous age slope rest on whichever studies sit at the extremes. A cell type with only a handful of cells will have an uninformative composition interval.

p_age <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, age_years) |>
  ggplot(aes(age_years)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 20, fill = "steelblue") +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Samples")

p_types <- obs_lung |>
  dplyr::count(cell_type_unified_ensemble, name = "n_cells") |>
  ggplot(aes(cell_type_unified_ensemble, n_cells)) +
  geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Cells")

p_age + p_types & theme_bw()

Exercise 2. How many distinct samples fall in each age_bin?

Solution 
obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, age_bin) |>
  dplyr::count(age_bin)

Both bins should contain donors. A bin with a handful of samples cannot support the age term once dataset_id is in the model.

Exercise 3. Cross-tabulate distinct samples by dataset_id and age_binary. Which studies contain donors of both age classes? A study that contains only one class cannot separate age from study, and both models below include dataset_id.

Solution 
obs_lung |>
  dplyr::distinct(sample_id, dataset_id, age_binary) |>
  dplyr::count(dataset_id, age_binary) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = age_binary, values_from = n, values_fill = 0)

A study with a zero in either age class does not identify an age effect on its own. The fixed dataset_id term uses the studies that contain both classes.
